text: This is the military-industrial complex. And you see, a president warned us about it in nineteen sixty-one. A general, no less.
Dwight Eisenhower. Five-star general. His farewell warning? Guard against unwarranted influence, by the military-industrial complex.
Where did it start? World War Two. Car plants built bombers. Willow Run: one B twenty-four an hour.
Then the Cold War arms race. Its spin-offs? Jet engines. Satellites. GPS. Arpanet, the internet's ancestor.
Today? World military spending: two point nine trillion dollars. A record, says Sipri.
Who gets the contracts? The top hundred arms makers: six hundred seventy-nine billion. Lockheed Martin leads.
Now explode one fighter jet. Engine. Radar. Wings. Chips. The F thirty-five alone? Over nineteen hundred suppliers.
And the climate? Militaries: maybe five and a half percent of global emissions. An estimate. Reporting is voluntary.
The new race? Drones and AI. Ukraine built about four million drones in twenty twenty-five.
Of course, the same machine also built GPS and the internet. Eisenhower's question still stands: who's steering it?
What should we take apart next?
